units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1:20">Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אם היה חותמה שׁוֹקֵעַ</he> if the seal on it was engraven, opp. <he>בולט</he>; <cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 5:2">Tosef. Ab. Zar. V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 6:2">VI</cite>), 2; Bab.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 43b">Ab. Zar. 43ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 19">Gen. R. s. 19</cite> (ref. to <he>לרוח היום</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 3:8">Gen. III, 8</cite>) <he>לרוח ששׁוֹקַעַת עם היום</he> by the (western) wind that goes down with the day.
<cite ref="Genesis 3:8">Ib.</cite> <he>כל שהיום שוקע וכ׳</he> the more the day goes down, the cooler it grows.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4:8">Y. Sabb. I, 3ᵈ</cite> top <he>אחד צף ואחד שוקע וכ׳</he> one kind of poison floats, another settles &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 10:1">Mikv. X, 1</cite> <he>צלוחית שפיה שוקע</he> a bottle the mouth of which is turned down.
Men. 103ᵇ, v. Hithpa.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 5:7">B. Mets. V, 7</cite> <he>מששְׁקָעוֹ בכבשן</he> after he let the lime stones down into the kiln (Y. ed. <he>משיִשְׁקַע כבשנו</he>, or <he>משיְשַׁקֵּעַ</he>) when he has filled his kiln).

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 966">Yalk. Koh. 966</cite>, v. <cite ref="U01214"><he>שָׁלָה</he></cite>; a. e.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U01836"><he>שָׁקוּעַ</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="U01837"><he>שְׁקוּעָה</he></cite> &c.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 43b">Bekh. 43ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H01714"><he>חָרַם</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ex. R. s. 15<sup>22</sup></cite> <he>והארץ ש׳ במים</he> the earth was submerged in water. Sifra Thazr., Par. 5, ch. XV (ref. to <he>פחתת</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 13:55">Lev. XIII, 55</cite>) <he>שיהיו כל מראיה שְׁקוּעִין</he> Rabad (ed. <he>שׁוֹקְעִין</he>) that all its colors appear lower (v. <cite ref="U01863"><he>שַׁקִּיעַ</he></cite>; cmp. <cite ref="P00874"><he>עָמוֹק</he></cite>); Yalk. Lev. 553 <he>שׁוֹקְעִין</he>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 7:1">Bekh. VII, 1</cite> <he>ראשו ש׳</he>, v. <cite ref="U01833"><he>שָׁקוּט</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 6:4">Snh. VI, 4</cite> <he>מְשַׁקְּעִין את הקורה וכ׳</he> they insert the trunk (of the gallows) in the ground. Y. Shek. V, end, 49ᵇ <he>כמה ממון שִׁיקְּעוּ אבותי כאן</he> how much money have my ancestors sunk here (in building that synagogue)!; <he>כמה נפשות שיקעו וכ׳</he> how many souls did thy ancestors sink here! were there no people to study the Law (on whom that money might have been spent)?; Y. Peah VIII, end, 21ᵇ.

B. Mets. V, 7 Y. ed., v. supra; a. e.—Trnsf. toembody in a collection without regard to original wording, to edit, abridge. Y. Hor. III, 48ᶜ top; Y. Sabb. XVI, 15ᶜ הדא דאת אמר עד שלא ש׳ בו רבי רוב משניות אבל משש׳ וכ׳ what you say (that the study of the Mishnah collection is preferable) refers to the time before Rabbi had embodied and abridged most of the Mishnayoth in his edition, but since then, run at all times after the Talmud (where the discussions are quoted in their original form).—Part. pass. מְשׁוּקָּע; f. מְשׁוּקַּעַת; pl. מְשׁוּקָּעִים, מְשׁוּקָּעִין; מְשׁוּקָּעוֹת.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:15">Koh. R. to I, 15</cite> <he>מקצתה מש׳ בארץ</he> part of the boat rests on dry land. Y. B. Mets. II, beg. 8ᵇ <he>במש׳ בו</he> when the objeot is found stuck in it, opp. <he>בנתון בו</he> when it is seen that it was put there.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33">Gen. R. s. 33</cite> <he>שהיתה התיבה מש׳ במים וכ׳</he> that the ark was eleven cubits in the water. Y. Yoma VII, beg. 44ᵃ <he>זרעו של דוד מש׳ שם</he> the seed of David is sunk there (in the family of the Resh Galutha). Y. Sabb. III, 6ᵃ top <he>כסא שרגליו מש׳ בטיט</he> a chair the feet of which stick in the mud. Y. Ḥag. I, 76ᵈ top; Y. Peah II, 17ᵃ <he>כמה … וכולהן מש׳ במשנה</he> many Hălakhoth have been communicated to Moses from Sinai, and they all are embodied in the Mishnah; a. e.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 68">Gen. R. s. 68</cite> <he>ה׳ הקב״ה גלגל וכ׳</he> the Lord caused the sun to set before its time.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 68:10">Ib.</cite> <he>מה אתה בצאתך הִשְׁקַעְתִּי חמה וכ׳</he> as I caused the sun to set when thou didst go out &c.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 21">Lev. R. s. 21</cite>; Pesik. Aḥăre, p. 176ᵃ <he>לעולם יַשְׁקִיעַ וכ׳</he> (Ar. s. v. <cite ref="T01146"><he>רתק</he></cite>: <he>יְשַׁקֵּעַ</he> or <he>יִשְׁקַע</he>) man should at all times sink himself into the study of the Mishnah, for when he knocks &c., v. <cite ref="T01146"><he>רָתַק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:5">Koh. R. to I, 5</cite> <he>עד שלא ה׳ שמשו … הזריח וכ׳</he> before God made the sun of Moses to set, he made the sun of Joshua to rise, v. <cite ref="U01542"><he>שֶׁמֶשׁ</he></cite>. Ib. 4 <he>היוצר הזה מַשְׁקִיעַ כבשונו מה שמשקיע וכ׳</he> the potter fills his oven; what he sinks into it first, is the last to come out; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be sunk, drowned; to be mixed up beyond recognition.
units: <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 22:11">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXII</cite> <he>המִשְׁתַּקְּעִים שוקעים את שוקעיהן</he> those that were to be drowned, drowned those that wanted to drown them.
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 2:24">Ruth R. to I, 17</cite> <he>נ׳ … בחליו</he> was three days unconscious on his sick-bed, opp. <he>נתישבה דעתו</he> he came to.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ex. R. s. 15<sup>6</sup></cite> <he>מִשְׁתַּקְּעִין בעונות וכ׳</he> are sunk in sins through the evil inclination.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ib</cite>.<sup>15</sup> <he>עד שנִשְׁתַּקְּעוּ תהומות</he> until the depths were filled with water. Y. Shek. VIII, beg. 51ᵃ <he>והיו עולי רגלים משתקעין וכ׳</he> the pilgrims sank in blood up to their knees; <cite ref="Menachot 103b:20">Men. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>שוקעין</he>; <cite ref="Tosefta Eduyot 3:2">Tosef. Eduy. III, 2</cite> <he>מפקיעין בדם וכ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (read: <he>מְשׁוּקָּעִין</he>; Var. <he>מְשַׁקְּעִין את ארכובותיהן</he>).
<cite ref="Arakhin 6b">Arakh. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שלא נ׳ שם וכ׳</he> as long as the name of its owner (that donated it) is not merged (but is still traceable).

<cite ref="Kiddushin 75a:20">Kidd. 75ᵃ</cite> <he>עד שיִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שם ע״א ממנו</he> until the name of idolatry has disappeared from him (until his idolatrous ancestry is no longer traceable). Y. Keth. I, 25ᵈ top <he>משפחה שנ׳ בה פסול וכ׳</he> if a genealogical blemish is mixed up in a family, you must investigate it back to four mothers; Y. Kidd. IV, 65ᵈ bot.

<cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>מה נאשה ונִשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בהן גדולי הדור</he> what can we do (with these families), since prominent men of the generation are mixed up with them? <cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>חמשת … וכולם נשתקעו בכהונה וכ׳</he> Pashhur ben Imer had five thousand slaves, and they are all mixed up with high priestly families; Y. Yeb. VIII, 9ᵈ top; (<cite ref="Kiddushin 70b:11">Kidd. 70ᵇ</cite> <he>נטמעו</he>). Tanḥ. Noah 5 the Lord supported Noah <he>שלא יִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ במעשה דור המבול</he> lest he sink down in (the mud of) the deeds of the generation of the flood; a. fr.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 301:3-4">Sifré Deut. 301</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 26:5">Deut. XXVI, 5</cite> <he>ויגר</he>) <he>מלמד … להִשְׁתַּקֵּע אלא לגור שם</he> this shows that he (Jacob) did not go down (to Egypt) to settle there as a citizen, but only to sojourn there.

senses.gloss: to be lost in forests, fields &c. Y. Ber. II, end, 5ᵈ ובשעה שהוא משתקע וכ׳ but when one is lost, he may even trespass on a field of crocus; (B. Kam. 81ᵃ תועה). Y. Ber. l. c.; Y. B. Bath. V, 15ᵃ bot. וראו … משתקע ובא כנגדן they saw R. J. b. P. having lost his way and coming (through fields) towards them.
